chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Yusuf, from Abu Abdullah al-Mumin, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'For the man who performs Hajj on behalf of another, what is his recompense and reward?' He said, 'For the one who performs Hajj on behalf of a man is the recompense and reward of ten Hajjs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Hajj on behalf of someone else?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the spiritual compensation for the agent performing Hajj on behalf of another, granting them the reward of ten independent pilgrimages. This ruling underscores the high merit of proxy worship in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing the performer's reward from that of the principal. It reflects the broader theological principle that good deeds can be transferred and multiplied through sincere agency.
